source.title: Understanding Generalization of Deep Neural Networks Trained with Noisy Labels
source.authors: Wei Hu; Zhiyuan Li; Ding-Li Yu

record.tranche_reason: Tests test performance across several noisy-label rates, bearing on V4, using regularized training and CIFAR-10 rather than the original random-label experiments.
record.gate_note: The introduction's statement that networks fit any labels cites Zhang et al. and is not this study's result. The study reports its own test accuracies across noise rates in Table 1; Figure 2 also shows training curves at noise rate 0.4, but without textual numeric results. No results test completely random labels, optimization time, unstructured inputs, or the V6 learning order.
record.test_reason: The study's ordinary-training baselines measure the test-error component of V4 across corruption rates. Its AUX and RDI performance comparisons primarily evaluate proposed mitigation methods and do not establish random-label memorization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that RDI and AUX are theoretically and empirically effective for noisy-label learning. Their guarantees rely on the NTK regime; explaining the observed effectiveness outside that regime remains future work.
record.recipe_differences: Uses label corruption on MNIST and CIFAR classification, with distance-to-initialization or auxiliary-variable regularization and test-accuracy evaluation. It does not reproduce the original random-label fitting experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise rate and loss/epoch-selection condition are varied in Table 1; test accuracies differ by method and condition.

fits_no_version.finding: AUX improves clean-test accuracy and largely closes the gap between last-epoch and best-epoch performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Per-example auxiliary variables can improve robustness to partially corrupted labels.

fits_no_version.finding: RDI and AUX yield clean-distribution generalization guarantees in the NTK regime.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: These particular regularizers enable generalization under specified label-noise and kernel assumptions.

record.problems: Table 1 reports test accuracy, not training error, for CIFAR-10 noise rates only through 0.6. The accompanying training curves at noise rate 0.4 are figure-only in the supplied text; the study itself notes that ResNet-34 is likely outside the NTK regime, so its effectiveness is not explained by the theory.
record.rows_left_out: No Table 1 results omitted. Figure 2's training and test curves at noise rate 0.4 are not included as rows because the supplied text gives no numeric values and describes no explicit numeric training-error outcome.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, near-zero training error with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, and chance test performance.
Relative training time for true versus random labels and convergence slowdown across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit throughout the corruption sweep and test performance reaching chance at fully random labeling are not established by the recorded results or readable figure values.
Whether weight decay, dropout and augmentation prevent completely random-label fitting, and effects of removing them on clean-label generalization.
Direct measurement separating the learning of shared real patterns from subsequent noisy-label memorization. Related-work statements cite another study.

missing.what: The binary-MNIST noise sweep includes ordinary GD and early-stopped GD test errors, providing another setting relevant to V4. The prose explicitly reports ordinary GD overfitting, but numerical curve values cannot be recovered from this text.

Binary-CIFAR ordinary-SGD training and test error trajectories at 20% corruption are omitted without declaration. They could establish training fit and its relationship to test deterioration if the plotted values are recovered. AUX training error includes auxiliary variables and must not be treated as network-only memorization.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's limits_scope verdict: unmeasured endpoints and training fit are untested components, not demonstrated failures. Figure 2 shows test accuracy during training, not training error. Table 1 values are transcribed correctly; the uncertainty symbol should be ±. CIFAR-10 corruption selects another class uniformly, so a corruption fraction is not identical to uniform relabeling over all ten classes. No readable result establishes or contradicts V6.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labels, chance test error, and fitting without changing architecture or training hyperparameters.
Training time relative to true labels and convergence speed as corruption rises.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit across noise levels, the all-corrupted endpoint, and test error reaching chance.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent random-label fitting, and whether removing them alone harms true-label generalization.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.
